finding.claim: [CONFIRMED by code reading; impact low] The LFS batch download path passes an unvalidated client-supplied oid into a filesystem open, letting an unauthenticated client probe existence of arbitrary absolute paths and block handler threads via FIFOs/devices. Repro: POST /objects/batch with {"operation":"download","objects":[{"oid":"/etc/passwd","size":1}]}; 'actions' response means the file exists and is readable, 'error 404' means it does not exist.
finding.source: JSON body of POST /objects/batch: objects[].oid (lfs_server.py:120). Unauthenticated endpoint.

trace.note: Reads Content-Length body and json.loads it; no schema validation.
oid taken from obj.get('oid'); only truthiness and size presence checked (line 123).
For download, calls self._object_exists(oid) with the raw oid.
_object_exists calls lfs_store.open_object(oid); only KeyError is caught.
_sha_path uses os.path.join; a final component starting with '/' discards the store root.
open(path,'rb') on the resulting absolute path.

finding.guards_checked: _is_valid_oid (lfs_server.py:46-48) is applied to the /objects/ GET, PUT and verify routes (lines 173, 198, 242) but NOT to the batch path. Batch returns only a boolean per oid, so this is an existence oracle, not a read. Server is documented as 'Simple LFS server for testing' (lfs_server.py:283) with no authentication, lowering real-world impact. LFSServer is a ThreadingHTTPServer (lfs_server.py:282), so a FIFO open blocks one thread per request. Directory or unreadable targets raise uncaught IsADirectoryError/PermissionError (minor).

finding.claim: [PLAUSIBLE, low-medium] The HTTP LFS client follows href URLs from the server's batch response without checking they share the configured endpoint's origin. A malicious or compromised LFS server can direct client requests, including PUTs of the user's object content, to arbitrary hosts the client can reach.
finding.source: Batch response JSON actions.download.href / actions.upload.href / actions.verify.href, controlled by the remote LFS server.
finding.sink: pool_manager.request('GET', download_url) (lfs.py:705); urlopen(Request(upload_url, data=content, method='PUT')) (lfs.py:749-757); urlopen(Request(verify_action.href, method='POST')) (lfs.py:766-772).

trace.note: Server-supplied action.header values merged into request headers.
pool_manager.request('GET', download_url) with no origin check.
Plain urlopen PUT of full object content to that URL.
verify href used for a POST carrying oid and size.

finding.guards_checked: _is_valid_lfs_url (lfs.py:380-396) validates only the configured endpoint URL, not server-returned hrefs. The download path checks size and SHA-256 (lfs.py:709-716) but only after the request has been sent. Upload content is sent before any response validation. Not verified: whether AuthCallbackPoolManager (client.py) attaches credentials proactively to cross-host requests; if it does, this becomes a credential-leak finding.

finding.claim: [PLAUSIBLE, low; requires a pre-existing symlink in the target directory; not reproduced] build_index_from_tree creates parent directories and writes blob contents without lstat-checking intermediate path components, so a pre-existing worktree symlink can redirect a checkout write outside the work tree (e.g. into .git/hooks).
finding.source: Tree entries being materialized (entry.path, entry.sha), together with any symlink already present in root_path from an earlier checkout.
finding.sink: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(full_path)) (index.py:2231-2232) and build_file_from_blob -> open(target_path,'wb') (index.py:1916), which follow symlinked parent directories.

trace.note: validate_path on the full entry path rejects .git/.. elements but does not inspect symlinks.
os.path.exists follows symlinks; os.makedirs on an existing symlinked dir succeeds with no lstat check.
open(target_path,'wb') writes through any symlinked parent.

finding.guards_checked: stash.py:70-107 _verify_leading_dirs lstat-checks each leading component and rejects symlinks (mirrors git CVE-2021-21300), but this guard is NOT used on the index.py checkout path. build_file_from_blob (index.py:1893-1910) replaces a symlink at the final path only, not intermediate components. update_working_tree (index.py:2806+) processes deletions (index.py:3003) before additions (index.py:3023), which mitigates the tree-switch variant. Validators (index.py:2019-2170) plus core.protectNTFS default True (porcelain/__init__.py:5482) block .git spellings but not symlinked parents. Not checked: whether any caller invokes build_index_from_tree on a non-empty directory where an attacker-controlled symlink could already exist.
